other.about: Ship manifest and crew roster (track MC): what is aboard a ship, station or site. Everyone and everything aboard is a record entry (an actor of kind person or cargo) with an aboard.on link, so moving someone or something is one dated change and the history keeps it. No game's rules: roles, kinds of being and goods are plain words a pack or the GM writes. Life support days come from the stores aboard and from who is awake, at the rates below per kind of being; a kind with no rates says so rather than borrowing a human's.

kept.describes: where this person or cargo is: the ship, station, site or place it is aboard or at
what this person does aboard, in the setting's own words (captain, pilot, passenger)
awake, in cold sleep, missing or dead
the kind of being this person is (human, or a pack's species); blank when not stated
this person's own age in years on the date it was set; it moves on while they are awake
what this cargo is: a store the life support reads (oxygen, water, food) or any goods in plain words
how much of it there is, in aboard.unit
the unit of aboard.amount: kg, t, m3, or a count such as crates
the share of oxygen and water the life support recovers on this ship or station, from 0 (none) to 1 (closed loop)

life_support.about: What one person of each kind of being uses a day, by store. A store is matched by aboard.what (oxygen, water, food). Cold sleep uses nothing from the stores (fudge register).

human.why: nominal crew member: oxygen breathed, water drunk and used to make up food, and packaged food, per crew member per day

sources.nasa-bvad-2018: Anderson, M. S., Ewert, M. K. and Keener, J. F. 2018, Life Support Baseline Values and Assumptions Document, NASA/TP-2015-218570/REV1. https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20180001338
